newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares surge nearly six pct.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares surge nearly six pct.

text.p: Istanbul shares surged an average 5.93 percent on Wednesday in a very strong reaction to Tuesday's 3.98 percent dive, amid heavy selective buying led by shares of largely state-owned firms, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed 4,733.73 points higher at 84,595.12. Trade volume was little changed at 28.11 trillion lira after Tuesday's 28.21 trillion.
Brokers said players focused on state shares amid renewed privatisation hopes. All listed public firms are on the government's 1997 privatisation programme.
State shares can move the market index sharply due to their high market capitalisations.

"I do not approve yesterday's and today's sharp movements. The possibility of a downtrend still exists because the market has not yet digested the recent rally," said Kursat Oral from Meksa securities.

The index had surged 29.3 percent from September 13 to October 23 in a strong uptrend, but has since drifted mostly between 81,000 and 84,000 as it failed in three attempts to pierce the critical 85,000 resistance.
It hit an all-time high close of 84,692.20 on November 11 and sank to 79,861.38 on Tuesday.

Actives were led by largely state-owned firms -- Turkish Airlines, up 6.5 percent at 24,500 lira, petroleum products distributor Petrol Ofisi, up 14.6 percent at 31,500 lira and flat steel producer Eregli, up 19 percent at 12,500 lira.
Utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 9.7 percent at 102,000 lira and Koc Holding, up 7.9 percent at 20,500 lira were the two most heavily traded private sector bluechips.
Trade in the most active five stocks made up 33.7 percent of the total turnover.
Of the 229 shares traded, gainers sharply outdid losers by 180 to 21 and 28 finished stable.
The 85-share industrial index soared 5.24 percent to 90,023.33 and the 15-share financial index shot up 7.52 percent to 80,569.81.
